prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on the recent price trend: the share price is 41.9% higher than a year ago. Also in its favour: over the past year the share did 44.1 percentage points better than the Nifty 50; the share price is close to its 52-week high; and sales grew 8% compared with a year earlier. Other areas on this side: growth, the balance sheet.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: free cash flow for the last financial year was negative: the business spent more than it generated. Also against it: return on capital employed is only -18.6%, a weak return on the money in the business; operating profit covers interest only -14.6 times, thin; and sales shrank 0.3% a year on average over three years. Other areas on this side: risk, the quality of the business, the balance sheet.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 5 points in favour and 8 against give more points against. The pool score is 17 of 100. The side that carries most weight is cash flow and the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Underweight with low confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
